_comment: Pinned versions of the binary components that ship inside the installer.
Asset names are written out in full rather than assembled from a template:
a template is how a CUDA build gets downloaded by accident, and a typo here
must fail the build instead of fetching the wrong file.
Sizes were read from the GitHub API on 2026-07-27 and are informational.
Text-to-speech for read-aloud (TTS-01). This is the ARCHIVED MIT build of
rhasspy/piper, chosen over the live OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl for two measured
reasons: the live project publishes only Python wheels (34.119.688 bytes,
no executable), and it is GPL-3.0 because it embeds espeak-ng. This one is
a native binary that fits the vendoring already here, and it is MIT.
Frozen since Nov 2023: no fix will come. The escape hatch is that a voice
is .onnx + .json - data - so replacing the engine later does not
invalidate what a user already downloaded.
